title: The 5 Longest Bones in Your Body, Ranked (#1 Holds You Up)

scenes.text: Three of your five longest bones are in your legs. Number one holds up your whole body.

scenes.label: Ulna · 11 in
scenes.text: Number five: the ulna, in your forearm. About eleven inches long in most adults.

scenes.label: Humerus · 12 in
scenes.text: Number four: the humerus, your upper arm bone. About twelve inches, the longest bone outside your legs.

scenes.label: Fibula · 14 in
scenes.text: Number three: the fibula, the thin bone beside your shin. Around fourteen inches, but much slimmer than its neighbor.

scenes.label: Tibia · 15 in
scenes.text: Number two: the tibia, your shin bone. About fifteen inches, the second-longest bone you own.

scenes.label: Femur · 18 in
scenes.text: Number one: the femur, your thigh bone. About eighteen inches in most adults, and the longest, strongest bone you have.

description:
The five longest bones in your body, ranked by average adult length.
Three of them are in your legs, and number one is about eighteen inches long.
Which bone did you think was number one?
first_comment: Did you expect the femur at number one? Which body part should we rank next?
